thread:
Riley M: hey team, i'm wrapping up my onboarding task and about to open my first PR. quick Qs: preferred branch prefix, when to mark as draft vs ready for review, required CI checks, and any tiny PR etiquette we follow?
Devex Bot: welcome Riley! :wave: Branches: feat/, fix/, chore/, hotfix/. include ticket: `feat/INC-123-brief-desc`. Draft for WIP or waiting on infra. ready when tests pass locally and description has testing steps. See CONTRIBUTING: https://git.redwood.ai/CONTRIBUTING.md
Nora S: formatting: run `pre-commit install` and `pre-commit run --all-files`. small PRs are easiest to review — prefer <300 LOC but it's okay if you explain larger changes. put an overview + testing instructions in the PR body.
Riley M: thanks — do we squash on merge?
Devex Bot: default: squash-and-merge. if you need to preserve commits (multi-step feature), add a note and request "no-squash" from maintainers.
Jun K: CI: every push triggers `ci/lint`, `ci/unit`, and `ci/integration-smoke`. integration runs are gated on main merges. If your change touches runtime, include a short perf note (p95 before/after) and a small repro script.
Infra Bot: reminder: if you change infra manifests, add `infra-review` label and wait for infra approval. for secrets or KMS changes, follow the private runbook and @mention infra on the PR.
Riley M: got it. any checklist i should paste in the PR body?
Nora S: yeah, a tiny checklist helps reviewers: 1) ticket link, 2) brief summary, 3) steps to test, 4) CI status, 5) rollout/rollback notes, 6) owners contacted. copy-paste this each time.
Riley M: perfect. i'll push a draft and drop link here for a quick sanity pass :pray:
Jun K: ping me for runtime touches early, happy to give feedback before formal reviews.
Devex Bot: automated note: please ensure `Allow edits from maintainers` is enabled so CI fixes can be applied.
Riley M: thanks all :smile:
